title: Cohort-aware per-sequence KV compacting + fidelity sampling for memory-sensitive workloads
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem statement:
- KV cache for long-context models consumes a large fraction of GPU memory for enterprise workloads (notably >30% in a 32k context run). This limits batch sizes and drives higher infra costs.

Goal:
- Build and evaluate a per-request/sequence fidelity sampler that chooses a compacting strategy for the KV cache (FP8/INT8/INT4/none) at request time to optimize peak GPU memory while bounding output quality regressions to an acceptable SLA (measured by task-level metric thresholds and human A/B).

Hypothesis:
- A cohort-aware sampler (using lightweight sequence-level features + runtime signals) can reduce average KV memory footprint by 35–55% across production-like traffic while keeping quality regressions below 1–2% on critical evals. Adaptive policies (multi-armed bandit) can recover from incorrect compaction choices quickly.

Experiment approach:
1) Offline sensitivity profiling:
   - Use a 3k-instance prompt corpus segmented into cohorts (instruction length, domain, token entropy, attention span).
   - For each model variant (v1.18 baseline, 1.19 candidate), measure per-cohort degradation for FP8, INT8, INT4 compaction using metrics: ROUGE/L, exact-match for QA, log-perplexity delta, and model-side confidence calibration.
2) Lightweight predictor/heuristic:
   - Train a tiny decision tree / logistic model on offline signals (first 32 tokens embedding norms, prefix token types, user cohort) to predict sensitivity. Also implement a low-cost heuristic fallback: "short instruction" => INT4 allowed, "high-ambiguity" => INT8 or FP8.
3) Runtime bandit controller:
   - Implement an epsilon-greedy bandit that explores FP8/INT8/INT4 with decaying epsilon per cohort, using a reward combining cost savings (memory units freed) and quality penalty (measured by automatic metrics like token-level perplexity + a fast reranker).
4) Integration with continuous batching + KV cache:
   - When compacting is chosen, perform in-place KV quantize/pack at kv-shard layer and update batch metadata so downstream runtime picks correct kernel path. Ensure KV sharding and cross-GPU transfers handle mixed compact formats with a lightweight header.
5) Safety, rollback, and fallback:
   - If the controller detects sudden increase in error rate or drift, automatically disable compaction for affected cohort for 10 minutes and escalate to a monitoring alert.

Success metrics:
- Memory: >=35% median reduction in active KV footprint across sampled traffic; >50% in long-context tail (>8k sequences).
- Latency: <=5% median latency delta for generation end-to-end (including quantize overhead).
- Quality: automated eval metric deltas <1.5% absolute for high-priority tasks; human A/B loss <1% preference for baseline.
- Stability: rollback incidents <=1 in 30 days in canary.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation of per-sequence compacting controller + bandit policy in runtime prototype.
- Offline sensitivity tables covering at least 6 cohorts and 3 model sizes.
- Canary deployment on 5% of traffic with dashboarded metrics (memory, latency, quality signals) and automated rollback rule.
- Documentation: Confluence design, API contract for compacted KV header, and operator runbook for incident response.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: Silent quality regressions on narrow downstream tasks. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, human eval gating, and automatic fallback.
- Risk: CPU overhead from per-request quantize step spikes latency. Mitigation: micro-bench quantize kernels + offload to asynchronous worker when safe.
- Risk: Complexity in mixed-format KV across GPUs. Mitigation: design simple canonical packed header and compatibility shim in network path.
notes: Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/KV+cohort+fidelity+sampling (internal). Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3128 (WIP).
